intro_md:
Fifty-one machine-learning research questions, each asking a model to propose a better scientific method than the published ones.

ML-Relay follows the design of MLS-Bench. Where ML engineering combines many techniques to push a metric on one dataset, ML science makes one atomic, generalisable contribution — a better loss, criterion, schedule, solver, search policy or architectural block — that transfers across models, data and tasks. Each task here isolates such a component inside a fixed, already-built research pipeline: the model edits one file within one line range, and everything else — data, training loop, evaluation — runs as it is. The published reference methods for the question are ported to the same pipeline and measured on it; they are anchors, not the assignment. A submission is scored by where it lands relative to the reference methods, per evaluation setting: the weakest reference anchors 0 and the **strongest reference anchors 10%** of the scale, so 90% of the range is headroom above the state of the field. The task score is the geometric mean across several genuinely different settings, so a component has to generalise to score well. Running every baseline inside the pipeline and checking that their order matches the literature is how each task earned its place: it proves the editable component is the one that matters and that a better method, once written, will be measured.

**Composition.** 37 of the 51 tasks are newly constructed for ML-Relay. The other 14 are drawn from MLS-Bench, selected for quality. MLS-Bench Lite, by contrast, consisted mainly of evaluation scaffolding; every task here poses a research question with measured anchors.

**What ships.** Fifty-one self-contained Harbor tasks under `tasks/`. Each holds `instruction.md` (the question, the editable file and range, the interface, the reference methods with citations, the metrics), `environment/` (a Dockerfile that builds the pipeline and fetches the task's data from public origins, plus the agent-start workspace), `tests/` (the evaluation, mounted only at verification) and `solution/` (an oracle that replays one reference method). Run a task with `harbor run -p tasks/<task>`.
